evidence_for.text: Linear stability across k-modes is governed by exact polynomial Routh-Hurwitz criteria, and relaxing the differential-diffusion constraint via a third immobile node provably expands the Turing cone by >10x (Marcon 2016, Scholes 2019, Tica 2024).
The one-order-of-magnitude tolerance (>=10x vs published ~63x ratio between 0.022% and 0.00035%) absorbs minor differences in steady-state solver tolerances.

evidence_against.text: Absolute Turing fractions around 3.5e-6 require >=5e6 Latin-hypercube samples and matching Hill-function parameterization (non-competitive vs competitive inhibition in Tica 2024 Table S5) to avoid Monte Carlo under-sampling.

problems.note: This is the cleanest computational replication in the packet because it requires only vectorized Jacobian eigenvalue algebra and published parameter bounds. The packet should explicitly note that finding non-trivial positive steady states for Hill kinetics at each Latin-hypercube sample is part of the Scholes/Tica denominator definition.

evidence_for.text: Primary morphometric measurements of periodic spacing and embryonic/adult domain size exist in open literature for mouse hair follicles (Sick 2006), palatal rugae (Economou 2012), mouse digits (Sheth 2012), Pomacanthus stripes (Kondo 1995), zebrafish stripes, and avian feather buds.

problems.note: The crux is normalizing body size to the exact embryonic stage when the pattern is laid down rather than adult size; otherwise an embryonic mouse hair follicle and an adult angelfish stripe lie on incomparable size axes. Thus the transducer test will reach a fast, decisive verdict—almost certainly proving that isotropic Meinhardt PDE reduces to a symmetric elementary CA class (like Rule 90/18) rather than chiral Rule 30 unless oblique wave travel or asymmetric coupling is present.
